Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment before booking the deep-dive with engineering: 

Summary from discovery:
- Primary use: patient-facing summarization + structured triage suggestions inside Luma’s provider portal.
- Expected QPS: ~40 avg with spikes to ~120 for peak hours.
- Typical prompt length: 150–350 tokens; responses average ~120 tokens.
- Compliance: PHI in prompts is possible — you flagged requirement for VPC/private deployment or strong KMS.

Integration & architecture points to clarify:
1) SDK + auth: Which auth flow would you prefer for the POC — API key vs OIDC? Any corporate SSO (SAML/Okta) constraints we should know about?
2) Structured output/tool calling: you mentioned needing a JSON schema output + ability to call your internal triage API when confidence > 0.8. We can enable function/tool-calling with schema enforcement; confirm example schema or we can iterate.
3) Embeddings & reranker: Is the primary retrieval vector DB hosted in your infra (e.g., Elastic/Chroma) or are you planning to use our managed embeddings pipeline?
4) Model routing & policy: From the call it sounds like you want low-latency defaults for UI (p99 target ~200ms) with a fallback to higher-quality model for batch offline jobs. Any hard cost targets or preferred regions (us-east, us-west)?

Attachments: I attached a short integration checklist and a sample policy playbook (simple YAML) to give visibility into config options.

Next steps I propose:
- Intro to Ben (solutions engineering) for a 45-minute architecture + SDK walkthrough — Ben can propose a model routing policy and sample SDK config.
- Share a quick example SDK snippet and an architecture diagram.
- Confirm whether you want a Hosted API POC or Redwood Private (VPC) right away (private will add deployment lead time).

Would Wednesday 9am PT work for a technical session?

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

Thanks Camila — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: target p99 for interactive UI should be <= 200ms. If that means using a tuned smaller model for the UI and falling back to the high-capacity model for background jobs, that’s fine.
- Throughput & tokens: ~40 QPS sustained, spike up to ~120. Typical token counts you noted are correct.
- Region: prefer us-east primary; us-west as secondary. EU not required for this initial POC.
- Auth: we prefer OIDC via Okta for production, but for POC an API key or short-lived token is acceptable. We will need SSO integration notes for procurement.
- Embeddings: we host our vector DB (currently using a managed PostgreSQL + pgvector for the prototype). We would like to evaluate Redwood’s managed embedding pipeline vs us hosting embeddings — cost and latency tradeoffs matter.

Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize vendor by end of July, POC in July.

Yes please loop Ben for the architecture call. Wed 9am PT works for the team.

Hi Samir / team —

Thanks for the context. Below are concrete proposals ahead of Wed’s call so you can review and flag anything we should prioritize: 

1) High-level routing & policy approach (goal: meet p99 <= 200ms for interactive UI, control cost for bulk jobs)
- Default route: redwood-small-v1 (quantized) in us-east for UI traffic — continuous batching tuned for 50–120ms median and p99 ~150–220ms depending on prompt length.
- Fallback chain: redwood-small-v1 -> redwood-medium-v1 (for slightly higher quality at moderate cost) -> redwood-large-v1 (fallback for highest quality, used sparingly or for async jobs).
- Cost policy: set token-based budget caps per-route with automatic downgrade to cheaper model when daily spend > threshold.
- Region policy: primary in us-east; auto-failover to us-west for availability zones only (not active-active initially).

2) SDK/auth patterns
- POC: API key (short expiry) for simplicity.
- Production: OIDC short-lived token exchanged from Okta SSO; optional mutual-TLS for Private deployments.
- Header example: Authorization: Bearer <OIDC-short-token> or X-Api-Key: <key> for POC.

3) Structured output & tool calling
- We recommend function/tool calling for calling your triage API. Use strict JSON-schema enforcement with a thin validation layer on Redwood’s side (we can reject malformed outputs).

4) Embeddings & reranker options
- Option A: Use your pgvector DB for vector search to keep vectors in your control. We provide server-side embedding generation and push (batch or streaming).
- Option B: Use Redwood-managed embeddings for lower operational overhead; we can provide vector store connectors (managed Chroma) and performance probes.

5) Sample routing policy (YAML) — included as inline sample. This is intentionally simple; the console can render this and allow per-route overrides.
# sample-policy-playbook.yml
routes:
  ui_interactive:
    model_preference: [redwood-small-v1, redwood-medium-v1, redwood-large-v1]
    latency_slo_ms: 200
    region: us-east
    fallback_on_error: true
    cost_threshold_daily_usd: 350
  batch_high_quality:
    model_preference: [redwood-large-v1]
    latency_slo_ms: 5000
    region: us-east
    schedule: nightly

6) Prefix caching & KV cache
- For templated prompts we can enable prefix KV caching to avoid recomputing tokens; this will significantly reduce token cost for repeated boilerplate.

7) POC plan & metrics
- 2-week POC: Week 1 deploy UI route using redwood-small-v1 (hosted) + embedding integration to your pgvector. Measure p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, cost per thousand tokens. Week 2 introduce reranker and fallback chain and run load tests to validate cost targets.

Attachments: arch-diagram.png, sample-policy-playbook.yml (included in the Drive link and attached here as stubs).

If helpful I can paste a short sample SDK config for routing once you confirm which model families you want to test in POC.

Cheers,
